Architectural Designs and Patterns

架构设计与模式

In this chapter, we dive into the world of architectural design and patterns. These models and patterns form the backbone of modern software systems. We will explore how these designs support scalability, maintainability, and efficient data handling in diverse applications. This chapter will not only equip you with theoretical foundations but also inspire practical applications and innovations in your system design endeavors.

在本章中，我们深入架构设计与模式的世界。这些模型与模式构成了现代软件系统的骨架。我们将探讨这些设计如何在多样的应用中支持可扩展性、可维护性以及高效的数据处理。本章不仅会为你打下理论基础，还会激发你在系统设计实践中的实际应用与创新。

We begin our journey with change data capture (CDC), a pivotal technique in data architecture used for capturing changes made to data in a database. Then, advancing into the realm of asynchronous communication patterns, we discuss the pub/sub architecture, in which publishers emit events without knowledge of the subscribers’ identities. We’ll look at how message brokers and message queues manage data flow across systems. Our focus will be on Apache Kafka, a high-throughput distributed messaging system, and we’ll illustrate its architecture and use cases for handling large-scale data streams.

我们的旅程从变更数据捕获（CDC）开始，这是数据架构中一项关键技术，用于捕获数据库中数据发生的变更。随后进入异步通信模式的领域，我们讨论发布/订阅（pub/sub）架构，在这种架构中发布者发出事件时并不知道订阅者的身份。我们将看看消息代理和消息队列如何管理跨系统的数据流。我们的重点是 Apache Kafka——一个高吞吐的分布式消息系统，并将说明其架构以及处理大规模数据流的用例。

In distributed systems, managing service interactions is critical. In this chapter, we will explore key architecture patterns for building scalable, resilient, and maintainable systems in modern cloud environments. We’ll compare the choreography (decentralized) and orchestration (centralized) management approaches, examining scenarios where each is most effective. We’ll then move on to big data architectures, covering foundational models like lambda, kappa, and data lake architectures, along with the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS), a distributed filesystem for handling massive datasets. We’ll also look at application architectures, comparing monolithic, N-tier, and microservice structures. Then, we’ll delve into event-driven systems, highlighting how they enable communication across decoupled services in response to real-time events.

在分布式系统中，管理服务间交互至关重要。本章我们将探讨在现代云环境中构建可扩展、有弹性、可维护系统的关键架构模式。我们将对比编排（choreography，去中心化）与编制（orchestration，集中式）两种管理方式，考察各自在哪些场景下最为有效。随后我们转向大数据架构，涵盖 lambda、kappa、数据湖等基础模型，以及用于处理海量数据集的分布式文件系统 HDFS。我们还会考察应用架构，对比单体、N 层和微服务结构。接着，我们将深入事件驱动系统，重点说明它们如何响应实时事件、在解耦的服务之间实现通信。

The architecture patterns in this chapter serve as the blueprints for designing systems for the various use cases covered in Part III.

Change Data Capture

CDC is a sophisticated approach to data integration that tracks and captures changes in data at the source database in real time. This method pushes changes to various destinations, including other databases, data warehouses, or even real-time processing engines. The essence of CDC is its ability to provide fresh data to different parts of an organization, thereby ensuring that all systems reflect the latest information.

CDC 是一种精巧的数据集成方法，它在源数据库处实时跟踪并捕获数据的变更。这种方法把变更推送到各种目的地，包括其他数据库、数据仓库，甚至实时处理引擎。CDC 的精髓在于它能为组织的不同部分提供新鲜数据，从而确保所有系统都反映最新的信息。

The need for real-time data processing drives organizations to adopt CDC. In an era where data is as valuable as oil, having the most updated data can significantly enhance operational efficiency and decision-making capabilities. Traditional batch-processing methods, while reliable, fail to meet the demands for immediacy in today’s fast-paced business environments. They often require scheduled downtime and can affect system performance during data extraction, which is not conducive to real-time responsiveness.

对实时数据处理的需求驱使组织采用 CDC。在这个数据如同石油般宝贵的时代，拥有最新的数据能显著提升运营效率和决策能力。传统的批处理方法虽然可靠，却无法满足当今快节奏商业环境对即时性的要求。它们往往需要计划好的停机时间，并在数据抽取期间影响系统性能，不利于实时响应。

In cases where organizations need real-time analytics, CDC can synchronize transactional databases (like an RDBMS) with data warehouses (e.g., Snowflake, Redshift). This allows data pipelines to continuously push fresh data from the transactional system to the warehouse, ensuring up-to-date insights without heavy ETL (extract, transform, and load) batch jobs. We’ll explore CDC further in Chapter 16, when we discuss handling the design of new post creation.

当组织需要实时分析时，CDC 可以把事务型数据库（例如 RDBMS）与数据仓库（例如 Snowflake、Redshift）同步起来。这让数据管道能持续地把新鲜数据从事务系统推送到仓库，无需繁重的 ETL（抽取、转换、加载）批处理作业即可保证洞察是最新的。我们将在第 16 章进一步探讨 CDC，届时会讨论处理“新帖子创建”的设计。

CDC offers numerous advantages over batch loading, especially in terms of real-time performance:

相较于批量加载，CDC 具有诸多优势，尤其是在实时性能方面：

  • Reduced latency. CDC enables almost instantaneous data updates, allowing businesses to react to changes swiftly, which is crucial for dynamic pricing, stock updates, or personalized customer interactions.
    更低延迟。CDC 几乎能瞬时完成数据更新，让企业能迅速应对变化，这对于动态定价、库存更新或个性化客户交互至关重要。
  • Lower costs and bandwidth usage. By transmitting only the changes made since the last transfer, CDC minimizes the bandwidth required and reduces the costs associated with data transfer.
    更低成本与带宽占用。由于只传输自上次传输以来发生的变更，CDC 把所需带宽降到最低，并降低了与数据传输相关的成本。
  • Increased system efficiency. Since CDC captures changes as they occur, it imposes minimal impact on the source systems, avoiding the intensive resource use associated with batch processes.
    更高系统效率。由于 CDC 在变更发生时即刻捕获，它对源系统造成的影响极小，避免了批处理进程那种密集的资源占用。
Page 208

Software architects can implement CDC using various techniques, each suited to different system architectures and performance requirements:

软件架构师可以使用多种技术来实现 CDC，每种技术适用于不同的系统架构和性能需求：

  • Audit-column-based CDC. Time-based audit columns are a simple yet powerful method of implementing CDC. Adding timestamp columns such as created_at and updated_at to database tables makes it possible to track when each record was inserted or last modified. This method is particularly effective for applications that require a historical audit trail of changes. Its primary advantage lies in its simplicity and low overhead since it leverages the inherent capabilities of most RDBMSs.
    基于审计列的 CDC。基于时间的审计列是一种简单却强大的 CDC 实现方法。在数据库表中添加 created_at、updated_at 这样的时间戳列，就能跟踪每条记录是何时插入或最后修改的。这种方法对于需要历史变更审计轨迹的应用尤为有效。它的主要优点在于简单、开销低，因为它利用了大多数 RDBMS 自带的能力。
  • Log-based CDC. Log-based CDC operates by reading transaction logs maintained by the database. Since these logs are designed to keep a record of all changes for data recovery and integrity, they serve as a reliable source for capturing data changes without additional overhead on the database itself. This method supports near real-time data integration, making it suitable for high-availability systems and those requiring immediate consistency across platforms. Tools like Debezium interface with these logs transparently, providing a seamless flow of data changes into various types of data sinks, such as Kafka and databases.
    基于日志的 CDC。基于日志的 CDC 通过读取数据库维护的事务日志来工作。由于这些日志本身就是为数据恢复和完整性而记录所有变更的，它们就成了捕获数据变更的可靠来源，而不会给数据库本身带来额外开销。这种方法支持近实时的数据集成，适用于高可用系统以及要求跨平台立即一致的系统。像 Debezium 这样的工具透明地对接这些日志，把数据变更无缝地流入各种数据汇，例如 Kafka 和数据库。
  • Table deltas. Table deltas involve capturing changes based on the comparison of table snapshots at different times. This approach is straightforward: by periodically taking full snapshots of a table and comparing these snapshots, we can derive the changes. This method might introduce delays and is more resource intensive, however; thus, it is generally suited for systems with lower transaction volumes or where real-time sync is not critical. Despite these drawbacks, it remains a viable option for batch-processing scenarios where system resources and processing windows are appropriately planned.
    表增量（Table deltas）。表增量通过对比不同时刻的表快照来捕获变更。这种方法很直接：定期对一张表做全量快照，再对比这些快照，就能推导出变更。不过，这种方法可能引入延迟，且更耗资源；因此它通常适用于事务量较低、或实时同步并非关键的系统。尽管有这些缺点，对于系统资源和处理窗口都经过妥善规划的批处理场景，它仍是一个可行的选择。
  • Trigger-based CDC. Trigger-based CDC uses database triggers to capture changes by automatically executing predefined procedures or SQL commands in response to events (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) occurring in a table. This method allows for immediate capture and custom handling of data changes, facilitating complex transformations or immediate checks during the data-capture phase. While this method is highly flexible and occurs in real time, managing database triggers can increase the load and complexity, especially in large-scale systems.
    基于触发器的 CDC。基于触发器的 CDC 利用数据库触发器来捕获变更：当表中发生事件（INSERT、UPDATE、DELETE）时，自动执行预定义的存储过程或 SQL 命令。这种方法能立即捕获并自定义处理数据变更，便于在数据捕获阶段进行复杂转换或即时校验。虽然这种方法高度灵活且实时发生，但管理数据库触发器会增加负载和复杂度，尤其是在大规模系统中。
An extension of log-based CDC, the stream-based CDC method formats log data into more consumable streams, making it easier for applications to process changes in real time. One such example is Amazon DynamoDB streams for publishing data updates in DynamoDB tables to different sources.
基于流的 CDC 是基于日志 CDC 的一种扩展，它把日志数据格式化为更易消费的流，让应用更容易实时处理变更。一个例子是 Amazon DynamoDB Streams，它用于把 DynamoDB 表中的数据更新发布到不同来源。
Page 209

In real-world applications, CDC is not just a data integration tool: it is part of a broader strategy to enhance data agility and accessibility across enterprises. With cloud platforms increasingly offering built-in support for CDC, its adoption is becoming more straightforward and accessible. Organizations can leverage CDC to maintain up-to-date data across distributed environments and thus improve analytical capabilities without significant overhead or complexities.

在实际应用中，CDC 不仅仅是一个数据集成工具：它是一项更广泛战略的一部分，用于提升整个企业的数据敏捷性和可访问性。随着云平台越来越多地内置对 CDC 的支持，采用它变得更加直接和容易。组织可以利用 CDC 在分布式环境中保持数据最新，从而在不付出大量开销和复杂度的情况下提升分析能力。

Publisher-Subscriber Architecture

Pub/sub architecture is a foundational model in event-driven programming that facilitates asynchronous communication among different parts of the system. This pattern is vital for applications where components need to interact efficiently without directly being linked to one another, thereby promoting loose coupling and scalable design.

发布/订阅架构是事件驱动编程中的一个基础模型，它促进系统不同部分之间的异步通信。当应用中的各个组件需要高效交互、却又不希望彼此直接耦合时，这种模式至关重要，它能促进松耦合和可扩展的设计。

Although it is often conflated with the observer pattern, the pub/sub architecture stands out for its inherent design philosophy and operational dynamics. The core difference between the two lies in the routing mechanism. In the observer design pattern, observers are aware of the subject and can directly register with it to receive updates. Communication is generally synchronous, and all observers are notified simultaneously through direct method calls.

虽然它常被与观察者模式混为一谈，但发布/订阅架构以其内在的设计哲学和运作机制而独树一帜。二者的核心区别在于路由机制。在观察者模式中，观察者知道主题（subject）的存在，并可以直接向它注册以接收更新。通信通常是同步的，所有观察者通过直接的方法调用同时收到通知。

The pub/sub model, on the other hand, abstracts the publisher from the subscribers through a broker or event bus, which handles the transmission of messages or events. The publishers send messages to an event channel without knowing the subscribers’ details, which in turn listen to the channel without knowing who the publisher is. This setup enables asynchronous communication and can support complex many-to-many interactions more seamlessly than the observer pattern can.

而发布/订阅模型则通过一个代理（broker）或事件总线把发布者与订阅者解耦开来，由后者负责消息或事件的传输。发布者把消息发送到一个事件通道，而并不知道订阅者的细节；订阅者则监听该通道，也不知道发布者是谁。这种设置实现了异步通信，并且比观察者模式更无缝地支持复杂的多对多交互。

Pub/sub architectures involve a broker and queue; let’s look at those components in more detail.

发布/订阅架构涉及代理和队列；下面我们更详细地看看这些组件。

Message Brokers

Message brokers are key components in pub/sub architectures that manage the transmission of messages between producers (publishers) and consumers (subscribers). They ensure that messages are appropriately routed, maintained, and delivered, even in complex distributed systems.

消息代理是发布/订阅架构中的关键组件，负责管理生产者（发布者）与消费者（订阅者）之间的消息传输。即使在复杂的分布式系统中，它们也能确保消息被恰当地路由、保存和投递。

A typical message broker architecture, as shown in Figure 8-1, involves queues that temporarily store messages and topics that categorize these messages. Publishers send messages to specific topics, while subscribers register their interest in one or more topics. The broker then ensures that messages from the relevant topics are delivered to the appropriate subscribers.

如图 8-1 所示，一个典型的消息代理架构包含临时存储消息的队列以及对消息进行分类的主题（topic）。发布者把消息发送到特定主题，而订阅者则登记自己对一个或多个主题的兴趣。代理随后确保相关主题的消息被投递到合适的订阅者。

Page 210

Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP) is an open standard for passing messages between applications or organizations with a focus on high interoperability and reliability. AMQP mandates the behavior of the message provider and broker to ensure consistent message delivery, thus making it a favored choice for systems requiring robustness and functional predictability.

高级消息队列协议（AMQP）是一个用于在应用或组织之间传递消息的开放标准，重点在于高互操作性和高可靠性。AMQP 规定了消息提供者和代理的行为，以确保一致的消息投递，因此它成为那些要求健壮性和功能可预测性的系统的青睐之选。

Message Queues

Message queues are a fundamental part of the messaging infrastructure that act as a temporary holding pen for messages waiting to be routed from publishers to subscribers, as shown in Figure 8-1.

消息队列是消息基础设施的基本组成部分，如图 8-1 所示，它充当一个临时暂存处，存放等待从发布者路由到订阅者的消息。

Apache Kafka, which we’ll look at in detail in the last section of this chapter, is a prominent example of a message queue system. It is designed to handle high volumes of data while supporting high-throughput applications. Kafka and similar technologies illustrate the evolving capabilities of message queues in modern system architectures, particularly in handling large-scale, real-time data feeds efficiently.

Apache Kafka 是消息队列系统的一个杰出范例，我们将在本章最后一节详细介绍它。它设计用于处理海量数据，同时支持高吞吐应用。Kafka 及类似技术展示了消息队列在现代系统架构中不断演进的能力，尤其是在高效处理大规模实时数据流方面。

The pub/sub architecture, facilitated by advanced message brokers and queue systems like Kafka, represents a powerful paradigm for building decoupled, scalable, efficient applications. This architecture not only supports a separation of concerns but also enhances the ability to handle asynchronous communications across different components of a software system. This approach is increasingly relevant in today’s distributed systems, where managing data flow efficiently and reliably is more critical than ever.

由 Kafka 等先进消息代理和队列系统所支撑的发布/订阅架构，代表了构建解耦、可扩展、高效应用的强大范式。这种架构不仅支持关注点分离，还增强了在软件系统不同组件之间处理异步通信的能力。在当今的分布式系统中，高效而可靠地管理数据流比以往任何时候都更关键，这种方法也因此变得愈发重要。

Choreography and Orchestration

In the design of distributed systems, particularly those employing microservices, methods of managing service interactions—namely, choreography and orchestration—play pivotal roles in defining system behavior and capabilities.

在分布式系统（尤其是采用微服务的系统）的设计中，管理服务间交互的两种方式——编排（choreography）与编制（orchestration）——在定义系统行为和能力方面扮演着关键角色。

Choreography

Choreography employs a decentralized approach to workflow management. In this model, each service knows what to do and when to do it based on the events it consumes. There is no central coordinator; instead, services perform their duties independently following the event notifications they receive. This method promotes loose coupling as services are designed to react to events rather than direct commands from a central authority. It enhances system scalability and resilience because services operate independently.

编排采用一种去中心化的工作流管理方式。在这种模型中，每个服务根据它所消费的事件知道该做什么、何时去做。没有中央协调者；相反，各服务根据收到的事件通知独立履行职责。这种方法促进了松耦合，因为服务被设计为对事件做出反应，而不是对来自中央权威的直接命令做出反应。由于服务独立运作，它增强了系统的可扩展性和弹性。

The lack of a central controller can make it difficult to enforce certain business rules and to monitor the overall flow of processes. Error handling and debugging can also become more complex because the distributed nature of the architecture scatters log entries and error reports across various services.

缺乏中央控制器，会使得强制执行某些业务规则、以及监控流程的整体流向变得困难。错误处理和调试也会变得更复杂，因为架构的分布式本质把日志条目和错误报告分散到了各个服务中。

A subpattern in choreography is choreographed asynchronous events. In this pattern, services emit and consume events through a central message bus, allowing for a loosely coupled system where services operate independently without needing to know the details of one another’s operations. This pattern is particularly useful in systems with a high volume of write operations, such as IoT data processing or real-time notification systems.

编排中的一个子模式是“编排出的异步事件”。在这种模式中，各服务通过一条中央消息总线发出并消费事件，从而形成一个松耦合系统，服务独立运作，无需了解彼此操作的细节。这种模式在写操作量大的系统中尤为有用，例如 IoT 数据处理或实时通知系统。

Advantages include scalability due to the decoupled nature and resilience against service failures as each service can operate autonomously. However, challenges arise in managing the overall system state, making it harder to trace and debug workflows since they are distributed across multiple services. These challenges can be solved by the orchestration paradigm.

其优点包括：由于解耦而带来的可扩展性，以及由于每个服务都能自治运作而带来的对服务故障的弹性。然而，在管理整体系统状态方面会出现挑战，由于工作流分布在多个服务上，跟踪和调试变得更困难。这些挑战可以由编制范式来解决。

Design problems like ecommerce platforms’ order-processing systems and hotel reservation systems can be addressed using choreography between services. We will discuss a similar pattern for managing booking confirmation and payment flow in Chapter 18. The booking system waits for customer payment and reacts to events such as PaymentProcessed to confirm the booking with a BookingConfirmed event. This event is further used by other services, such as the billing system, to generate an invoice.
诸如电商平台的订单处理系统、酒店预订系统之类的设计问题，可以通过服务之间的编排来解决。我们将在第 18 章讨论一种类似的模式，用于管理预订确认和支付流程。预订系统等待客户付款，并对诸如 PaymentProcessed 之类的事件做出反应，以发出 BookingConfirmed 事件来确认预订。该事件还会被其他服务（例如账单系统）进一步使用，以生成发票。
Page 212

Orchestration

Orchestration, in contrast to choreography, relies on a central coordinator, or an orchestrator, which controls the interaction between services by making decisions about the process flow, directing different services when to act. This approach simplifies monitoring and managing business logic, which can be advantageous for complex business processes that require precise coordination and strict compliance to workflows. It also simplifies error handling and recovery since the orchestrator can keep track of process states and make decisions accordingly.

与编排相反，编制依赖一个中央协调者（orchestrator），它通过对流程流向做出决策来控制服务之间的交互，指挥不同服务在何时行动。这种方式简化了对业务逻辑的监控和管理，对于那些需要精确协调、严格遵守工作流的复杂业务流程来说是有利的。它还简化了错误处理和恢复，因为编制器可以跟踪流程状态并据此做出决策。

Multiple orchestration solutions are available as open source software and managed services by cloud providers, including Conductor and Maestro designed by Netflix, Temporal workflow orchestrator, AWS Step Functions, and Apache Airflow. We’ll discuss Step Functions and Airflow in Chapter 12.
有多种编制方案以开源软件和云厂商托管服务的形式提供，包括 Netflix 设计的 Conductor 和 Maestro、Temporal 工作流编制器、AWS Step Functions 以及 Apache Airflow。我们将在第 12 章讨论 Step Functions 和 Airflow。

Orchestration can lead to increased coupling between services as they rely on a central point for directions. This can also become a single point of failure, potentially affecting the system’s resilience and scalability. Orchestration can be implemented in various patterns, each suited to different workflow requirements and system architectures.

编制会导致服务之间耦合增加，因为它们依赖一个中心点来接受指令。这个中心点也可能成为单点故障，从而影响系统的弹性和可扩展性。编制可以用多种模式实现，每种模式适用于不同的工作流需求和系统架构。

Design problems like managing a video-upload feature on YouTube and Netflix can be easily managed via orchestration platforms. Each step in the workflow invokes a specific service to perform a task, such as validating, encoding, and distributing video. We’ll discuss this in much more detail in Chapter 20.
诸如管理 YouTube 和 Netflix 上视频上传功能之类的设计问题，可以很容易地通过编制平台来管理。工作流中的每一步都会调用某个特定服务来执行一项任务，例如校验、转码和分发视频。我们将在第 20 章更详细地讨论这一点。

Orchestrated, synchronous, and sequential pattern

In this pattern, the orchestrator sends synchronous requests to services in a sequential manner, waiting for each response before proceeding to the next step. This approach is suitable for workflows that are complex and involve multiple steps that need to be completed in a specific order, such as ecommerce checkout processes.

在这种模式中，编制器以顺序方式向服务发送同步请求，每收到一个响应才进行下一步。这种方式适用于复杂、且包含多个必须按特定顺序完成的步骤的工作流，例如电商结账流程。

Advantages of this pattern include centralized control, which makes managing complex workflows easier, and easier debugging because of the explicit workflow definition in the orchestrator. However, the system can face challenges, such as a single point of failure in the orchestrator and potential performance bottlenecks due to the sequential execution of tasks.

这种模式的优点包括：集中式控制，使复杂工作流更容易管理；以及由于工作流在编制器中有显式定义而更容易调试。然而，系统也会面临挑战，例如编制器成为单点故障，以及由于任务顺序执行而可能出现性能瓶颈。

Orchestrated, synchronous, and parallel pattern

Similar to the sequential approach but with parallel execution of independent tasks, this pattern improves performance and reduces latency. It is effective in scenarios where multiple services can be called simultaneously, such as in data-aggregation services.

这种模式与顺序方式类似，但对独立任务进行并行执行，从而提升性能、降低延迟。它在可以同时调用多个服务的场景中很有效，例如数据聚合服务。

Page 213

Advantages of this pattern include improved performance by reducing the overall time to complete workflows and flexibility in managing workflows that involve both parallel and sequential steps. However, challenges can be the increased complexity of managing parallel operations and the risk of resource contention if services are not optimized for parallel execution.

这种模式的优点包括：通过缩短完成工作流的总时间来提升性能，以及在管理同时包含并行和顺序步骤的工作流时具有灵活性。然而，挑战在于管理并行操作的复杂度会增加，以及如果服务没有针对并行执行做优化，就存在资源争用的风险。

Orchestrated, asynchronous, and sequential pattern

In this pattern, the orchestrator sends asynchronous requests, allowing services to process tasks independently and return results via callbacks or message queues. This approach is ideal for systems with long-running tasks where services need to continue processing without waiting for responses, such as in batch-processing systems.

在这种模式中，编制器发送异步请求，允许服务独立处理任务，并通过回调或消息队列返回结果。这种方式非常适合那些包含长时间运行任务、且服务需要继续处理而不必等待响应的系统，例如批处理系统。

Advantages of this pattern include better handling of long-running processes without blocking resources and increased system resilience since services can retry operations on failure. However, challenges arise from the increased complexity of managing asynchronous responses and the need for additional mechanisms to handle eventual consistency and failure recovery.

这种模式的优点包括：能更好地处理长时间运行的进程而不阻塞资源，以及由于服务在失败时可以重试操作而增强了系统弹性。然而，挑战在于管理异步响应的复杂度增加，并且需要额外的机制来处理最终一致性和故障恢复。

Hybrid orchestration and choreography pattern

This pattern combines the strengths of both choreography and orchestration by using orchestration for explicit workflows and choreography for implicit, event-driven operations. It is useful in complex systems where some workflows require strict control, while others benefit from decentralized execution, such as in large-scale distributed applications.

这种模式结合了编排和编制两者的长处：对显式工作流使用编制，对隐式的、事件驱动的操作使用编排。它在复杂系统中很有用——其中某些工作流需要严格控制，而另一些则受益于去中心化执行，例如大规模分布式应用。

In a large ecommerce platform, the order-processing service acts as the orchestrator, controlling the main steps of the workflow: verifying payment, reserving inventory, confirming the order, and initiating shipment. This explicit orchestration ensures that the core order workflow remains tightly controlled, with each step executed in a specific order, which is essential for transaction integrity and reliability. Alongside the orchestrated core, various supporting services use a decentralized, event-driven approach. For example, when an order is shipped, an event is emitted. Independent services, like the notification service and the analytics service, listen to this event and perform their respective tasks (sending notifications to the customer and updating delivery statistics) without direct coordination, allowing for flexibility and scalability.

在一个大型电商平台中，订单处理服务充当编制器，控制工作流的主要步骤：核验支付、预留库存、确认订单、发起发货。这种显式编制确保核心订单工作流处于严密控制之下，每一步都按特定顺序执行，这对于事务完整性和可靠性至关重要。在被编制的核心之外，各种支撑服务采用去中心化、事件驱动的方式。例如，当订单发货时，会发出一个事件。独立的服务（如通知服务和分析服务）监听该事件，各自执行自己的任务（向客户发送通知、更新配送统计），而无需直接协调，从而获得灵活性和可扩展性。

Advantages of this pattern include the flexibility to handle diverse workflow requirements and improved system resilience by leveraging both centralized and decentralized approaches. However, challenges are the complexity of ensuring clear boundaries between orchestrated and choreographed operations and the risk of overlapping responsibilities leading to inefficiencies.

这种模式的优点包括：能够灵活处理多样的工作流需求，以及通过同时利用集中式和去中心化方式来增强系统弹性。然而，挑战在于要确保编制操作与编排操作之间边界清晰相当复杂，并且职责重叠可能导致低效。

Page 214

Deciding Between Choreography and Orchestration

The decision to use choreography or orchestration largely depends on specific project requirements. Choreography is better suited to systems where high scalability and resilience are necessary and where business processes can be adequately handled with a decentralized approach. Orchestration is preferable for complex processes requiring tight control and coordination across multiple services, where the business logic is too intricate to be effectively managed through a decentralized approach. Both approaches have their place in system design, and understanding their strengths and limitations is crucial for architects to design solutions that not only meet current needs but also are adaptable to future demands and changes in business processes.

选择编排还是编制，很大程度上取决于具体的项目需求。编排更适合那些需要高可扩展性和弹性、且业务流程可以用去中心化方式妥善处理的系统。编制则更适合那些需要跨多个服务严密控制和协调的复杂流程——其业务逻辑过于复杂，无法通过去中心化方式有效管理。两种方式在系统设计中都有其位置，理解它们的长处和局限，对于架构师设计出不仅满足当前需求、还能适应未来需求和业务流程变化的方案至关重要。

As enterprises continue to generate exponentially growing volumes of data, the big data architectural strategies to store, process, and analyze such vast datasets become increasingly important, so we will look at those in the next section.

随着企业持续产生指数级增长的数据量，用于存储、处理和分析如此庞大数据集的大数据架构策略变得愈发重要，因此我们将在下一节探讨它们。

Big Data Architecture

Big data architectures are designed to effectively handle the challenge of the 5 Vs of data—volume, velocity, variety, veracity, and value—ensuring that organizations can derive actionable insights and maintain performance scalability. Big data architectures have evolved from traditional databases to large data warehouses and data lakes. We’ll discuss three models for modern big data architecture based on how they have evolved.

大数据架构旨在有效应对数据的 5 个 V 带来的挑战——规模（volume）、速度（velocity）、多样（variety）、真实（veracity）和价值（value）——确保组织能够得出可落地的洞察，并保持性能的可扩展性。大数据架构已经从传统数据库演进到大型数据仓库和数据湖。我们将根据现代大数据架构的演进方式，讨论三种模型。

Lambda Architecture

Lambda architecture, illustrated in Figure 8-2, is a hybrid data-processing model that combines both batch and real-time processing methods.

如图 8-2 所示，lambda 架构是一种混合数据处理模型，同时结合了批处理和实时处理两种方式。

This architecture is designed to balance latency, throughput, and fault tolerance by processing and presenting data in these three layers:

这种架构通过以下三层处理和呈现数据，来平衡延迟、吞吐量和容错性：

  • Batch layer. This layer handles large volumes of data in batches, processing historical data stored over extended periods. It provides comprehensive and accurate views but with higher latency. The batch layer is responsible for creating precomputed views that store the results of the batch processing.
    批处理层。这一层以批处理方式处理海量数据，处理长期存储的历史数据。它提供全面而准确的视图，但延迟较高。批处理层负责创建预计算视图，用于存储批处理的结果。
  • Speed layer. For real-time data processing needs, the speed layer processes data as it arrives, ensuring low latency. This layer compensates for the high latency of the batch layer by providing timely—albeit potentially approximate—views.
    速度层。对于实时数据处理的需求，速度层在数据到达时即刻处理，确保低延迟。这一层通过提供及时（尽管可能是近似的）视图，来弥补批处理层高延迟的不足。
Page 215
  • Serving layer. The final component, the serving layer, merges output from both the batch and the speed layers to present a coherent view of results to the end users.
    服务层。最后一个组件是服务层，它合并批处理层和速度层两者的输出，向终端用户呈现一个连贯的结果视图。

Lambda architecture is beneficial for scenarios where it is crucial to have a near real-time view of data but also to handle massive datasets that are not feasible to process quickly. The two components—batch and speed layers— introduce an additional complexity of operational management. This limitation can be solved by kappa architecture, which combines both into a single system.

Lambda 架构适用于这样的场景：既要近乎实时地查看数据，又要处理那些无法快速处理的海量数据集。批处理层和速度层这两个组件带来了运维管理上的额外复杂度。这个局限可以由 kappa 架构解决——它把两者合并成一个系统。

Kappa Architecture

An evolution of lambda architecture, kappa architecture simplifies operational complexity by treating all incoming data as a stream. This model, shown in Figure 8-3, proposes using a single processing layer (the stream-processing layer) for both real-time and historical data. By treating all data as a stream, kappa architecture removes the need to maintain two separate codebases and systems for batch and real-time processing, simplifying development and maintenance.

Kappa 架构是 lambda 架构的演进，它把所有进入的数据都当作流来处理，从而简化运维复杂度。如图 8-3 所示，这种模型建议用单一处理层（流处理层）同时处理实时数据和历史数据。通过把所有数据都视为流，kappa 架构省去了为批处理和实时处理维护两套独立代码库和系统的需要，从而简化了开发和维护。

This architecture leverages advanced stream-processing tools that can handle time windowing, event ordering, and state management across potentially unbounded datasets. Kappa architecture is particularly suitable for applications where the input data is naturally streaming or where fast data recency is more critical than computing-intensive, complex batch analytics.

这种架构利用先进的流处理工具，这些工具能够在可能无界的数据集上处理时间窗口、事件排序和状态管理。Kappa 架构特别适用于这样的应用：输入数据本身就是流式的，或者数据的新鲜度比计算密集型的复杂批分析更重要。

Page 216
The idea here is to simplify the batch and streaming workloads into a single pipeline, but implementation and productionization can vary depending on the organization’s use case. Uber leverages kappa architecture to solve multiple problems, such as dynamic ride pricing, fraud detection, and user experience analytics. A single pipeline is designed to address these different use cases with easy switching between batch and streaming workloads.
这里的思路是把批处理和流处理负载简化为单条管道，但具体实现和生产化方式会因组织的用例而异。Uber 利用 kappa 架构解决了多个问题，例如动态打车定价、欺诈检测和用户体验分析。单条管道被设计用来应对这些不同用例，并能在批处理与流处理负载之间轻松切换。

Data Lake Architecture

Data lakes are centralized repositories designed to store, process, and secure large volumes of structured and unstructured data. Unlike traditional data warehouses, which generally store data in a structured, processed format, data lakes retain vast amounts of raw data in its native format. This approach, illustrated in Figure 8-4, offers a few distinct advantages, including scaling out using low-cost hardware, flexible configuration of the data lake’s organization, indexing and processing logic, and storage support for and analysis of a wide variety of data types, including logs, XML, JSON, and binary formats. Data lake architecture not only supports big data storage but also integrates with various big data processing frameworks to enable comprehensive analytics and machine learning directly on the stored data.

数据湖是集中式存储库，旨在存储、处理并保护海量结构化和非结构化数据。传统数据仓库通常以结构化、已处理的格式存储数据，而数据湖则以原始格式保留海量原始数据。如图 8-4 所示，这种方式具有若干独特优势，包括：利用低成本硬件横向扩展；对数据湖的组织方式、索引和处理逻辑进行灵活配置；以及支持存储和分析种类繁多的数据类型，包括日志、XML、JSON 和二进制格式。数据湖架构不仅支持大数据存储，还能与各种大数据处理框架集成，直接对所存储的数据进行全面分析和机器学习。

You can also use object storage solutions like Amazon S3 to build data lake architectures. S3 offers easy integration with big data services like Amazon EMR, AWS Glue, and Amazon Athena to run big data workloads. We’ll discuss these services in much more detail in Chapter 13.
你也可以使用像 Amazon S3 这样的对象存储方案来构建数据湖架构。S3 能与 Amazon EMR、AWS Glue、Amazon Athena 等大数据服务轻松集成，以运行大数据负载。我们将在第 13 章更详细地讨论这些服务。
Page 217

By implementing big data architectures such as lambda, kappa, and data lake, organizations can effectively manage their data ecosystems to support both current analytical needs and future data-driven initiatives. This ensures that the infrastructure not only meets the technical requirements of big data processing but also aligns with strategic business objectives.

通过实施 lambda、kappa、数据湖等大数据架构，组织可以有效地管理其数据生态，既支持当前的分析需求，也支持未来的数据驱动计划。这确保基础设施不仅满足大数据处理的技术要求，还与战略业务目标保持一致。

While big data architecture is primarily concerned with processing and managing large volumes of data efficiently, application solution system design focuses on creating systems that meet specific business requirements and integrate various components. The next section will contrast solution architecture designs with the data-centric approaches of big data architecture.

大数据架构主要关注高效处理和管理海量数据，而应用解决方案系统设计则专注于创建满足特定业务需求、并集成各种组件的系统。下一节将把解决方案架构设计与大数据架构以数据为中心的方式做对比。

Solution Architecture

Solution architecture has evolved from monolithic architectures to microservices, reflecting shifts in technology and business requirements. This section provides an overview of this evolution and these architectures, exploring their configurations and the principles behind their designs.

解决方案架构已经从单体架构演进到微服务，反映了技术和业务需求的转变。本节概述这一演进过程以及这些架构，探讨它们的配置及其设计背后的原则。

Monoliths

In a monolithic architecture, shown in Figure 8-5, all components of the software application are tightly integrated and run as a single service. This means that any changes made anywhere in the application can affect the entire system, which simplifies development and deployment processes in the early stages of a product’s lifecycle.

如图 8-5 所示，在单体架构中，软件应用的所有组件都紧密集成在一起，作为单一服务运行。这意味着应用中任何地方所做的改动都可能影响整个系统，但在产品生命周期的早期阶段，这反而简化了开发和部署流程。

Page 218

Monoliths are straightforward to develop, test, deploy, and scale horizontally since they are a single executable or deployment unit. This is a very big advantage over microservices because the network interactions between different microservices are skipped, which helps reduce latency and provides easier handling of unreliable networks.

单体应用易于开发、测试、部署和横向扩展，因为它们是单一可执行文件或部署单元。相比于微服务，这是一个巨大优势，因为省去了不同微服务之间的网络交互，有助于降低延迟，并且更容易应对不可靠的网络。

However, as applications grow, monoliths can become unwieldy and difficult to understand and modify. Scaling specific functions of the application rather than the entire application can also become challenging. From a scalability standpoint, we recommend keeping the code decoupled and modular so that it can be deployed separately if necessary. Even if the code is deployed in a single repository, modular code architecture allows you to reuse the components or add new features easily, and it maintains the code readability to proper standards. The next section describes this pattern in more detail.

然而，随着应用增长，单体会变得笨重，难以理解和修改。想要只扩展应用的某些特定功能而非整个应用，也会变得有挑战。从可扩展性的角度，我们建议保持代码解耦和模块化，以便在必要时可以单独部署。即使代码部署在单一仓库中，模块化的代码架构也让你能复用组件或轻松添加新功能，并把代码可读性维持在恰当的水准。下一节将更详细地描述这种模式。

N-tier Architectures

N-tier architectures break an application down into logical layers, each with a specific responsibility. Typically, these include at least three layers: presentation (frontend), business logic (middle-tier), and data management (backend). This is referred to as three-tier architecture, illustrated in Figure 8-6.

N 层架构把应用拆分为若干逻辑层，每一层都有特定职责。通常至少包含三层：表示层（前端）、业务逻辑层（中间层）和数据管理层（后端）。这被称为三层架构，如图 8-6 所示。

This architecture enhances maintainability by separating concerns among components, making it easier to manage, update, and scale individual parts of the system without affecting others. This architecture choice provides scalability and flexibility since each layer can be scaled independently according to demand. For instance, the data layer can be scaled up to handle larger data loads without necessarily scaling the presentation layer.

这种架构通过在组件之间分离关注点来增强可维护性，使得管理、更新和扩展系统的各个部分变得更容易，而不会影响其他部分。这种架构选择提供了可扩展性和灵活性，因为每一层都可以根据需求独立扩展。例如，可以扩展数据层以处理更大的数据负载，而不必扩展表示层。

While N-tier architectures provide a significant improvement over monolithic designs by separating concerns, modern applications often require even greater flexibility, scalability, and fault tolerance. This is where microservices come into play.

虽然 N 层架构通过分离关注点相比单体设计有了显著改进，但现代应用往往需要更强的灵活性、可扩展性和容错能力。这时微服务就登场了。

Page 219

Microservices

A microservice architecture, illustrated in Figure 8-7, takes the principles of N-tier systems further by decomposing them into smaller, loosely coupled services. Each microservice focuses on a single functionality and can be developed, deployed, and scaled independently.

如图 8-7 所示，微服务架构把 N 层系统的原则进一步推进，将其分解为更小、更松耦合的服务。每个微服务专注于单一功能，可以独立开发、部署和扩展。

The microservice architecture offers several benefits and challenges. It gives teams autonomy to develop, test, deploy, and scale services independently, speeding up development cycles and improving fault isolation. It also allows for technology diversity, enabling different services to use the best-suited technology stack for their specific tasks.

微服务架构带来若干好处，也带来若干挑战。它赋予团队自主地独立开发、测试、部署和扩展服务的能力，加快了开发周期，并改善了故障隔离。它还允许技术多样性，让不同服务可以为自己的特定任务使用最合适的技术栈。

However, the decentralized nature of microservices increases the complexity of management and operations, particularly with regard to interservice communications, data consistency, and transaction management. Additionally, service overhead can grow since each service may require its own database, libraries, and dependencies, increasing the resource footprint and management effort.

然而，微服务的去中心化本质增加了管理和运维的复杂度，尤其是在服务间通信、数据一致性和事务管理方面。此外，服务开销可能增长，因为每个服务都可能需要自己的数据库、库和依赖，从而增加资源占用和管理工作量。

Page 220

Transitioning from a monolithic to a microservice architecture may not suit every project or organization and should be approached with a clear understanding of the associated trade-offs. Issues like network latency, message formats, data integrity, and transaction management require robust strategies, such as API gateways, service meshes, and comprehensive logging and monitoring systems, to ensure system reliability and performance. By carefully evaluating the needs of the business and the capabilities of the team, organizations can choose the most appropriate architecture to support their goals, ensuring that their software infrastructure is both effective today and adaptable for future needs.

从单体架构过渡到微服务架构未必适合每个项目或组织，应当在清楚理解相关取舍的前提下进行。像网络延迟、消息格式、数据完整性和事务管理这类问题，需要稳健的策略来应对，例如 API 网关、服务网格以及全面的日志和监控系统，以确保系统的可靠性和性能。通过仔细评估业务需求和团队能力，组织可以选择最合适的架构来支撑自己的目标，确保其软件基础设施在当下既有效、又能适应未来的需求。

Another interesting paradigm for implementing application or big data architecture is event-driven architecture (EDA).

实现应用或大数据架构的另一个有趣范式是事件驱动架构（EDA）。

Event-Driven Architecture

EDA is a paradigm that orchestrates behavior around the production, detection, and consumption of events. This model offers a dynamic framework for applications to react to various state changes across distributed systems without the tight coupling of components, promoting scalability and responsiveness. We will start with EDA concepts and implementation paradigms and then go into the details of event sourcing specifically.

EDA 是一种围绕事件的产生、检测和消费来组织行为的范式。这种模型为应用提供了一个动态框架，使其能够在分布式系统中对各种状态变化做出反应，而无需组件之间紧密耦合，从而促进可扩展性和响应能力。我们将从 EDA 的概念和实现范式讲起，然后专门深入事件溯源的细节。

EDA Concepts and Implementations

An event-driven system enables the components of an application to communicate based on events rather than direct calls or shared-state manipulation. This is often realized by using events as messages that might be persisted until processed. Such systems leverage a state-machine approach. Here are the main concepts in this approach:

事件驱动系统让应用的组件基于事件进行通信，而不是基于直接调用或对共享状态的操作。这通常是通过把事件当作消息来实现的，这些消息可能会被持久化，直到被处理。这类系统利用状态机方法。下面是这种方法中的主要概念：

  • State machine. A mathematical abstraction used to design algorithms based on a behavior model. A state machine reads a set of inputs and changes to a different state based on those inputs.
    状态机。一种数学抽象，用于基于行为模型设计算法。状态机读取一组输入，并根据这些输入切换到不同状态。
  • State. A description of the status of a system waiting to execute a transition.
    状态。对系统等待执行一次转换时所处状况的描述。
  • Transition. A change from one state to another. A transition is a set of actions to execute when a condition is fulfilled or an event is received.
    转换。从一个状态到另一个状态的变化。转换是在某个条件被满足、或收到某个事件时要执行的一组动作。
  • Event. The entity that drives the state changes.
    事件。驱动状态变化的实体。
Page 221
  • Event-driven state machine. A state machine is event-driven if the transition from one state to another is triggered by an event or a message (not based on consuming or parsing characters or based on conditions).
    事件驱动状态机。如果状态机从一个状态到另一个状态的转换是由一个事件或一条消息触发的（而不是基于消费或解析字符、也不是基于条件），那么它就是事件驱动的。

Paradigms of Event-Driven Implementations

EDA is about implementing components that communicate via publishing events rather than making, for example, RPC/CRUD calls against one another or manipulating shared state. It’s a communication strategy (albeit one that often relies on messages being persisted for fairly long periods until they are consumed). The two major implementation styles for EDA are state-oriented implementation and event sourcing.

EDA 关注的是实现这样的组件：它们通过发布事件来通信，而不是彼此进行 RPC/CRUD 调用或操作共享状态。它是一种通信策略（尽管这种策略常常依赖消息被持久化相当长一段时间，直到被消费）。EDA 的两种主要实现风格是面向状态的实现和事件溯源。

  • State-oriented implementation. This method involves capturing the current state only, focusing on persisting state changes over time. State data is treated as mutable within controlled limits, modified only through defined operations, which makes the system responsive but tightly bound to current state conditions without historical tracking.
    面向状态的实现。这种方法只捕获当前状态，专注于随时间持久化状态变更。状态数据在受控范围内被视为可变，只能通过定义好的操作来修改，这使得系统响应迅速，但紧紧绑定于当前状态条件，而没有历史追踪。
  • Event sourcing. Unlike state-oriented implementations, event sourcing persists each state change as an immutable event. These events are the system’s source of truth, from which the current state can be reconstructed. This approach supports historical state reconstruction, auditing, and complex system behaviors like rollback and replay of events to handle errors or system failures.
    事件溯源。与面向状态的实现不同，事件溯源把每次状态变更都持久化为一个不可变事件。这些事件是系统的事实来源（source of truth），可以从中重建当前状态。这种方法支持历史状态重建、审计，以及回滚、事件重放等复杂系统行为，以处理错误或系统故障。

Event sourcing allows for the following:

事件溯源带来以下能力：

  • Complete rebuilds. Enables systems to discard and rebuild state from scratch by replaying events.
    完全重建。让系统能够通过重放事件，丢弃状态并从头重建。
  • Temporal queries. Inspects a state at any point in time by reprocessing events up to that moment.
    时间查询。通过重新处理截止到某个时刻的事件，来查看该时刻的状态。
  • Event replays. Corrects errors by reprocessing events after correcting them or adding new ones.
    事件重放。通过在更正事件或新增事件之后重新处理它们来修正错误。

Event-driven systems often use an event store, an append-only persistence optimized for storing events in sequence, as a single source of truth about the operations on both the application state and the data. This store ensures that all events are captured immutably, providing a reliable foundation for triggering actions, building projections, or reconstructing past states. These systems decouple data changes from application logic, allowing systems to scale and adapt more flexibly to changing business requirements.

事件驱动系统通常使用事件存储（event store）——一种为按顺序存储事件而优化的只追加（append-only）持久化——作为关于应用状态和数据操作的单一事实来源。这种存储确保所有事件都被不可变地捕获，为触发动作、构建投影或重建过去状态提供可靠基础。这些系统把数据变更与应用逻辑解耦，让系统能更灵活地扩展和适应不断变化的业务需求。

Page 222

An event-sourced persistence will model the entities as event streams and keep an immutable journal of these event streams. When the entity state or attribute mutates, it produces and saves a new event. When the entity state needs to be restored, all the events for that entity are read, and each event is applied to change the state, reaching the correct final state of the entity. Note that state here is the pure function application of the event stream on the entity.

事件溯源式的持久化会把实体建模为事件流，并为这些事件流保留一本不可变的日志。当实体状态或属性发生变化时，它就产生并保存一个新事件。当需要恢复实体状态时，就读出该实体的所有事件，并逐个应用这些事件以改变状态，最终达到实体正确的最终状态。注意，这里的状态就是事件流在实体上的纯函数应用结果。

When implementing event sourcing in event-driven systems, there are several important factors to consider:

在事件驱动系统中实现事件溯源时，有几个重要因素需要考虑：

  • Eventual consistency. Reads may not reflect the most recent writes immediately because of delays in creating materialized views or projections. During the time between event publication and view creation, new events may be added to the event journal.
    最终一致性。由于创建物化视图或投影存在延迟，读操作可能不会立即反映最近的写入。在事件发布与视图创建之间的这段时间里，事件日志中可能又加入了新事件。
  • Event log immutability. The event log should be immutable, meaning events cannot be updated once written. To correct a previous event, a new event must be added. Any changes to the event schema must be applied consistently across all stored events.
    事件日志不可变性。事件日志应当不可变，即事件一旦写入就不能再修改。要更正之前的事件，必须新增一个事件。对事件模式（schema）的任何变更，都必须一致地应用到所有已存储的事件上。
  • Event ordering and linearity. Maintaining the correct order of events is crucial for data consistency, especially when multiple publishers are involved. Adding timestamps or incremental identifiers to events can help resolve ordering conflicts.
    事件顺序与线性。保持事件的正确顺序对数据一致性至关重要，尤其是在涉及多个发布者时。给事件加上时间戳或递增标识符，有助于解决顺序冲突。
  • Consumer idempotency. Since events might be delivered more than once, consumers must be idempotent, meaning they should be able to handle duplicate events without applying the same update multiple times, which could lead to incorrect state changes.
    消费者幂等性。由于事件可能被投递不止一次，消费者必须是幂等的，也就是说它们应当能够处理重复事件，而不会多次应用同一次更新（否则可能导致错误的状态变更）。
  • Snapshotting and materializing. Regular snapshotting and materializing of events are necessary, especially when dealing with large event streams. This helps manage on-demand queries and ensures efficient access to the current state of the model.
    快照与物化。定期对事件做快照和物化是必要的，尤其是在处理大型事件流时。这有助于管理按需查询，并确保高效访问模型的当前状态。

Because of the decentralized control over the application’s flow and the distributed nature of event handling, you’ll need to keep these practical considerations for eventual consistency in mind and manage the complexity when architecting event-driven systems.

由于对应用流程的控制是去中心化的、事件处理又是分布式的，在设计事件驱动系统时，你需要把这些关于最终一致性的实际考量牢记在心，并管理好其中的复杂度。

Event-driven architecture represents a paradigm shift from traditional request-driven models, providing a flexible, scalable way to handle asynchronous system behaviors and data flows. This architectural style is particularly well suited to applications where scalability, responsiveness, and robustness are crucial, such as in microservice environments or systems requiring complex business processes and workflows.

事件驱动架构代表了从传统请求驱动模型的一次范式转变，为处理异步系统行为和数据流提供了一种灵活、可扩展的方式。这种架构风格特别适合那些可扩展性、响应能力和健壮性至关重要的应用，例如微服务环境，或需要复杂业务流程和工作流的系统。

Page 223
Event sourcing and CDC both track changes in data, but they serve different purposes. Event sourcing captures all changes as events that can re-create or revert the system’s state over time, essentially using events as the source of truth. In contrast, CDC primarily focuses on capturing changes made to a database to replicate or integrate data, using the database’s transaction logs to record state changes without inherently storing the intent or context of the changes.
事件溯源和 CDC 都跟踪数据变更，但二者用途不同。事件溯源把所有变更都捕获为事件，可以随时间重建或回退系统状态，本质上是把事件当作事实来源。相比之下，CDC 主要专注于捕获对数据库所做的变更，以复制或集成数据，它利用数据库的事务日志记录状态变更，而并不内在地存储变更的意图或上下文。

Common Cloud Architecture Patterns

In this section, we explore essential cloud architecture patterns that form the backbone of scalable, resilient, maintainable systems in cloud environments. These patterns—ranging from resilience-focused techniques like the circuit breaker to transaction-handling strategies like saga orchestration—will provide you with foundational tools that are especially valuable in the system design use cases presented in Part III. Understanding these patterns will better equip you to apply robust, tested solutions to common challenges in distributed architectures, setting the stage for effective design decisions.

在本节中，我们探讨重要的云架构模式，它们构成了云环境中可扩展、有弹性、可维护系统的骨架。这些模式——从断路器这类以弹性为重点的技术，到 saga 编制这类事务处理策略——将为你提供基础工具，它们在第三部分给出的系统设计用例中尤其有价值。理解这些模式，能让你更好地把经过验证的稳健方案应用到分布式架构的常见挑战上，为有效的设计决策打下基础。

Event-Based Patterns: CQRS and Saga

Event-based architectures leverage the following patterns to manage distributed transactions and operations:

基于事件的架构利用以下模式来管理分布式事务和操作：

  • Command query responsibility segregation (CQRS). CQRS is an architectural pattern that separates the operations that read data (queries) from the operations that update data (commands) into different interfaces. This separation allows read and write operations to be handled differently, optimizing performance, scalability, and security. For example, read models can be scaled independently from write models, which is particularly beneficial in systems where the number of read operations vastly exceeds the number of write operations.
    命令查询职责分离（CQRS）。CQRS 是一种架构模式，它把读取数据的操作（查询）与更新数据的操作（命令）分离到不同接口中。这种分离让读操作和写操作可以被区别处理，从而优化性能、可扩展性和安全性。例如，读模型可以独立于写模型进行扩展，在读操作数量远超写操作数量的系统中尤其有益。
  • Saga. Sagas manage transactions that span multiple services, where each transaction step is paired with a compensating action for rollback if needed. They are based on either choreography or orchestration. In choreography, each service involved in the saga performs its transaction and publishes events that trigger the next steps in other services. In orchestration, a central coordinator (the orchestrator) directs each step of the saga, managing the sequence and triggering compensating transactions if necessary.
    Saga。Saga 管理跨多个服务的事务，其中每个事务步骤都配对一个补偿动作，以便在需要时回滚。它们基于编排或编制。在编排方式中，参与 saga 的每个服务执行自己的事务，并发布事件以触发其他服务中的下一步。在编制方式中，一个中央协调者（编制器）指挥 saga 的每一步，管理执行顺序，并在必要时触发补偿事务。
Page 224

These patterns are crucial in environments where distributed transactions need to be managed across microservices, providing a structure for handling complex operations reliably and efficiently.

在需要跨微服务管理分布式事务的环境中，这些模式至关重要，它们为可靠而高效地处理复杂操作提供了一种结构。

Failure-Tolerant Patterns: Circuit Breaker, Retry with Backoff, and Rate Limiter

To enhance system resilience in the face of failures, employ the following patterns:

为在故障面前增强系统弹性，请采用以下模式：

  • Circuit breaker. The circuit breaker pattern prevents a cascade of failures in distributed systems. When a particular service or operation fails to a threshold level, the circuit breaker “trips,” and further attempts to invoke the failing service are halted temporarily, thus allowing it to recover and maintain system stability.
    断路器。断路器模式防止分布式系统中出现故障级联。当某个特定服务或操作的失败达到阈值时，断路器就“跳闸”，暂时停止进一步调用该故障服务，从而让它得以恢复并维持系统稳定。
  • Retry with backoff. Retry with backoff involves reattempting failed operations with increasing delays between attempts, increasing the interval (backoff) progressively with each retry until a maximum number of retries is reached. This pattern is particularly useful when handling transient faults by providing time for the issue to resolve before retrying.
    带退避的重试。带退避的重试是指：以逐渐增大的重试间隔重新尝试失败的操作，每次重试都逐步拉长间隔（退避），直到达到最大重试次数。这种模式在处理瞬时故障时尤其有用，因为它在重试之前给问题留出了自行解决的时间。
  • Rate limiter. The rate limiter pattern controls the number of requests to a service within a specified time frame, preventing the system from being overwhelmed by a high volume of traffic or sudden spikes in demand. Rate limiting can be applied at various levels: per user, per service, or globally across a system. This pattern ensures that services continue to operate smoothly even under heavy load, reducing the likelihood of degraded performance or system crashes due to resource exhaustion.
    限流器。限流器模式控制在指定时间范围内发往某个服务的请求数量，防止系统被海量流量或突发需求峰值压垮。限流可以在多个层面应用：按用户、按服务，或在整个系统范围内。这种模式确保服务即使在高负载下也能平稳运行，降低因资源耗尽而导致性能下降或系统崩溃的可能性。

These patterns work together to prevent cascading failures in distributed systems, ensuring that failures in one part of the system do not lead to widespread outages.

这些模式协同工作，防止分布式系统中的故障级联，确保系统某一部分的故障不会导致大范围宕机。

Domain-Based Patterns: Domain-Driven Design and Decompose by Subdomains

The following patterns focus on aligning software design with business objectives:

以下模式专注于让软件设计与业务目标保持一致：

  • Domain-driven design (DDD). DDD focuses on the core domain logic and its complexity, basing the design on the domain’s behavior and logic. This pattern encourages the creation of a domain model that incorporates business rules and behaviors, leading to a more intuitive correlation between the software and the business requirements it aims to fulfill.
    领域驱动设计（DDD）。DDD 专注于核心领域逻辑及其复杂性，把设计建立在领域的行为和逻辑之上。这种模式鼓励创建一个融入业务规则和行为的领域模型，从而让软件与其要满足的业务需求之间形成更直观的对应关系。
Page 225
  • Decompose by subdomains. Decompose by subdomains builds on DDD in a microservice architecture to divide a system into subdomains, each handling a specific business capability. Each microservice manages a subdomain, which improves maintainability and scalability by allowing the microservice to evolve independently based on its unique business requirements.
    按子域分解。按子域分解在微服务架构中以 DDD 为基础，把系统划分为若干子域，每个子域负责一项特定业务能力。每个微服务管理一个子域，这通过让微服务根据其独特业务需求独立演进，从而提升可维护性和可扩展性。

These patterns are essential for building modular, scalable systems that can evolve as business needs change.

这些模式对于构建模块化、可扩展、并能随业务需求变化而演进的系统至关重要。

API Routing Strategies and Patterns

API routing patterns determine how requests are directed within cloud environments to the appropriate services. These patterns are essential to ensuring that requests reach the correct backend systems efficiently and securely. Common routing strategies include:

API 路由模式决定了在云环境中如何把请求导向合适的服务。这些模式对于确保请求高效而安全地到达正确的后端系统至关重要。常见的路由策略包括：

  • Hostname routing. This strategy routes requests to different backend systems based on the hostname in the URL. It is commonly used in scenarios where multiple services are hosted under different subdomains or domains.
    主机名路由。这种策略根据 URL 中的主机名把请求路由到不同的后端系统。它常用于多个服务托管在不同子域或域名之下的场景。
  • Path routing. This routing pattern uses URL paths to direct requests to specific services or handlers. It allows for clear, organized routing based on the structure of the URL, making it easier to manage and scale services.
    路径路由。这种路由模式使用 URL 路径把请求导向特定服务或处理器。它允许基于 URL 的结构进行清晰、有条理的路由，使服务更易于管理和扩展。
  • HTTP header routing. In this approach, HTTP headers within the request are leveraged to make routing decisions. This is particularly useful for scenarios like A/B testing, where different user groups are directed to different backend services, or for gradual rollouts of new features.
    HTTP 头路由。在这种方式中，利用请求中的 HTTP 头来做出路由决策。它在 A/B 测试等场景中特别有用——把不同用户组导向不同后端服务；或者用于新功能的灰度发布。

API routing architecture involves either an API gateway or service mesh in microservice-based systems:

在基于微服务的系统中，API 路由架构要么采用 API 网关，要么采用服务网格：

  • API gateway. An API gateway acts as a centralized entry point for all client requests, providing a unified interface to a set of backend services. It handles tasks such as request routing, composition, and protocol translation. The API gateway can invoke multiple microservices to fulfill a single client request and aggregate the responses into a cohesive result. This pattern is particularly useful in microservice architectures as it simplifies client interactions and enhances security by centralizing access control and monitoring.
    API 网关。API 网关充当所有客户端请求的集中入口，为一组后端服务提供统一接口。它处理请求路由、组合和协议转换等任务。API 网关可以调用多个微服务来完成单个客户端请求，并把响应聚合成一个内聚的结果。这种模式在微服务架构中特别有用，因为它简化了客户端交互，并通过集中化访问控制和监控来增强安全性。
Page 226
  • Service mesh. Service mesh architecture is an infrastructure layer that manages service-to-service communication within a microservice architecture. It provides advanced routing, load balancing, service discovery, and security features like mutual Transport Layer Security (TLS) authentication and traffic encryption. Unlike API gateways, which handle external client-to-service communication, service mesh focuses on internal service-to-service interactions, ensuring reliable, secure communication within the cloud environment. It is implemented using sidecar proxies that intercept and manage network traffic between services, providing observability and resilience without requiring changes to the application code.
    服务网格。服务网格架构是一个基础设施层，负责管理微服务架构内部服务之间的通信。它提供高级路由、负载均衡、服务发现，以及双向传输层安全（TLS）认证、流量加密等安全特性。与处理外部“客户端到服务”通信的 API 网关不同，服务网格专注于内部“服务到服务”的交互，确保云环境内通信可靠、安全。它通过 sidecar 代理实现，这些代理拦截并管理服务之间的网络流量，在不修改应用代码的情况下提供可观测性和弹性。

These API routing strategies and patterns, along with the API gateway and service mesh architectures, are foundational to building scalable, secure, and maintainable cloud native applications.

这些 API 路由策略和模式，连同 API 网关和服务网格架构，是构建可扩展、安全、可维护的云原生应用的基础。

Other Cloud Architecture Patterns

In addition to the essential patterns, several other cloud architecture patterns address specific challenges and enhance system design:

除了这些重要模式之外，还有若干其他云架构模式用于应对特定挑战、增强系统设计：

  • Anticorruption layer. The ACL serves as a protective barrier that prevents potentially disruptive data or requests from entering a system segment, thereby preserving the integrity of an application’s core business model. It acts as a translator between different subsystems or external applications, ensuring that data exchanges do not corrupt the domain model.
    防腐层（ACL）。防腐层充当一道保护屏障，阻止具有潜在破坏性的数据或请求进入某个系统区段，从而保护应用核心业务模型的完整性。它在不同子系统或外部应用之间充当翻译器，确保数据交换不会破坏领域模型。
  • Strangler fig pattern. This pattern is used for gradually transforming legacy systems by replacing specific pieces of functionality with new applications and services. Over time, these new components “strangle” the old system, eventually replacing it entirely.
    绞杀者模式（Strangler fig）。这种模式用于逐步改造遗留系统：用新应用和新服务替换其中特定的功能片段。随着时间推移，这些新组件逐渐“绞杀”旧系统，最终将其完全取代。
  • Transactional outbox. The transactional outbox pattern is used to ensure reliable messaging between services. When changes are made to the database, records are also added to an “outbox” table within the same transaction. A separate process then sends these messages to the message queue or other destinations, ensuring data consistency across service boundaries.
    事务性发件箱（Transactional outbox）。事务性发件箱模式用于确保服务间消息传递的可靠性。当对数据库做变更时，记录也会在同一事务中被加入一张“发件箱”表。随后由一个独立进程把这些消息发送到消息队列或其他目的地，从而跨服务边界保证数据一致性。
  • Sidecar pattern. The sidecar pattern is commonly used in microservice architectures. It involves deploying an additional container or process alongside a service container, providing platform-connected services such as monitoring, logging, configuration, and networking capabilities. The sidecar can be written in any language without strong dependency on the main container and thus provides decoupling. This pattern allows for isolating infrastructure concerns from the application, making it cleaner and more modular.
    Sidecar 模式。Sidecar 模式常用于微服务架构。它是在一个服务容器旁边再部署一个额外的容器或进程，提供与平台相连的服务，例如监控、日志、配置和联网能力。Sidecar 可以用任意语言编写，不与主容器强耦合，从而提供解耦。这种模式把基础设施关注点与应用隔离开来，让应用更干净、更模块化。
Page 227
  • Backend for frontend (BFF). This pattern involves creating separate backend services tailored for different types of clients, such as desktop browsers and mobile devices. It allows developers to optimize these backend services for specific user interfaces, enhancing the user experience by reducing overfetching or underfetching of data.
    后端 for 前端（BFF）。这种模式为不同类型的客户端（例如桌面浏览器和移动设备）创建各自独立、量身定制的后端服务。它让开发者可以针对特定用户界面优化这些后端服务，通过减少数据的过度获取或获取不足来提升用户体验。
  • Cellular architecture. Cellular architecture involves designing systems as collections of cells, where each cell operates independently but can communicate with other cells. Each cell is self-contained with its own data store and logic, capable of scaling autonomously. This approach is highly resilient since failure in one cell does not affect the others, and it supports evolutionary architecture by allowing each cell to evolve independently.
    单元化架构（Cellular）。单元化架构把系统设计为若干单元（cell）的集合，每个单元独立运作，但可以与其他单元通信。每个单元是自包含的，有自己的数据存储和逻辑，能够自主扩展。这种方式弹性极高，因为一个单元的故障不会影响其他单元；它还通过让每个单元独立演进来支持演进式架构。

Each of these patterns provides targeted solutions to common problems in developing and managing cloud native applications, offering pathways to more resilient, flexible, and scalable architectures. Remember, this is not an exhaustive list of architecture patterns, and the list keeps evolving with the latest developments in system design. However, these patterns together offer robust solutions to various architectural challenges that you might face when designing complex systems.

这些模式中的每一个都为开发和管理云原生应用中的常见问题提供了有针对性的解决方案，为通向更有弹性、更灵活、更可扩展的架构提供了路径。请记住，这并不是架构模式的穷举清单，而且随着系统设计的最新发展，这个清单还在不断演进。然而，这些模式合在一起，为你在设计复杂系统时可能遇到的各种架构挑战提供了稳健的解决方案。

Open Source Distributed Systems Architecture

Distributed systems architecture involves dividing responsibilities across multiple computing nodes to ensure that a system is scalable, fault tolerant, and efficient. In this context, we will explore two core components: distributed filesystems and distributed message queues, with a focus on open source implementations like HDFS for filesystems and Kafka for message queues.

分布式系统架构涉及把职责划分到多个计算节点上，以确保系统可扩展、容错且高效。在此语境下，我们将探讨两个核心组件：分布式文件系统和分布式消息队列，重点关注开源实现——文件系统以 HDFS 为代表，消息队列以 Kafka 为代表。

HDFS

HDFS is an open source filesystem designed to run on commodity hardware. It is highly fault tolerant and is designed to be deployed on low-cost hardware. HDFS provides high-throughput access to application data and is suitable for applications that require processing of large datasets. Here are some key features of HDFS:

HDFS 是一个开源文件系统，设计为在商用硬件上运行。它具有高容错性，并被设计为部署在低成本硬件上。HDFS 提供对应用数据的高吞吐访问，适用于需要处理大型数据集的应用。下面是 HDFS 的一些关键特性：

Page 228
  • Distributed storage. HDFS is engineered for scalability, distributing data across multiple nodes in a cluster. It breaks large files into blocks and replicates them across different machines, ensuring data redundancy and availability even in the event of hardware failures.
    分布式存储。HDFS 为可扩展性而设计，把数据分布到集群中的多个节点上。它把大文件切分成块，并在不同机器上复制这些块，即使发生硬件故障也能确保数据冗余和可用性。
  • Fault tolerance. One of the key features of HDFS is its built-in fault tolerance. Data is automatically replicated, typically across three different nodes, ensuring that if one node fails, the data remains accessible from the other nodes. This replication mechanism provides reliability and high availability, making HDFS well suited for large-scale data storage.
    容错性。HDFS 的关键特性之一是其内置的容错能力。数据会被自动复制，通常跨三个不同节点，确保即使某个节点故障，数据仍可从其他节点访问。这种复制机制提供了可靠性和高可用性，使 HDFS 非常适合大规模数据存储。
  • Scalability and flexibility. HDFS can scale horizontally by adding more nodes to the cluster, allowing it to manage increasing data volumes without significant changes to the infrastructure. This scalability, combined with its ability to store data in various formats, makes HDFS a flexible solution for a wide range of data-processing needs.
    可扩展性与灵活性。HDFS 可以通过向集群添加更多节点来横向扩展，从而在不对基础设施做重大改动的情况下管理不断增长的数据量。这种可扩展性，加上它能以多种格式存储数据的能力，使 HDFS 成为应对广泛数据处理需求的灵活方案。
  • High throughput. HDFS is optimized for high throughput, prioritizing data access speed over low latency. It is designed to handle large datasets with a focus on batch processing, making it ideal for big data applications that involve reading and writing large volumes of data.
    高吞吐量。HDFS 针对高吞吐量做了优化，把数据访问速度置于低延迟之上。它设计用于处理大型数据集、以批处理为重点，因此非常适合那些需要读写海量数据的大数据应用。
  • Cost-effectiveness. By using commodity hardware, HDFS provides a cost-effective solution for storing and processing large volumes of data.
    成本效益。通过使用商用硬件，HDFS 为存储和处理海量数据提供了一种高性价比的方案。
  • Integration with Hadoop ecosystem. HDFS is deeply integrated with the broader Hadoop ecosystem, supporting various processing frameworks like MapReduce, Hive, and Spark. This integration allows for seamless data processing and analysis, leveraging HDFS’s distributed architecture to perform computations close to the data, which can reduce network bottlenecks and improve efficiency.
    与 Hadoop 生态集成。HDFS 与更广泛的 Hadoop 生态深度集成，支持 MapReduce、Hive、Spark 等各种处理框架。这种集成让数据处理和分析可以无缝进行，利用 HDFS 的分布式架构把计算移近数据执行，从而减少网络瓶颈、提升效率。
AWS offers Amazon Elastic MapReduce (EMR), a managed service that simplifies running big data frameworks like Hadoop, including HDFS, on the AWS cloud. We will explore it further in Chapter 13. Amazon EMR supports processing vast amounts of data using HDFS (or EMRFS), leveraging its scalability, fault tolerance, and integration with the broader Hadoop ecosystem.
AWS 提供 Amazon Elastic MapReduce（EMR），这是一项托管服务，能简化在 AWS 云上运行 Hadoop（包括 HDFS）等大数据框架。我们将在第 13 章进一步探讨它。Amazon EMR 支持使用 HDFS（或 EMRFS）处理海量数据，充分利用其可扩展性、容错性以及与更广泛 Hadoop 生态的集成。
Page 229

HDFS architecture

The HDFS architecture, shown in Figure 8-8, is built around several key components that work together to provide a distributed, fault-tolerant, scalable filesystem.

如图 8-8 所示，HDFS 架构围绕若干关键组件构建，这些组件协同工作，提供一个分布式、容错、可扩展的文件系统。

The components of the HDFS architecture are:

HDFS 架构的组件包括：

  • NameNode. The NameNode is the central component of HDFS, responsible for managing the metadata and namespace of the filesystem. It keeps track of file locations and manages access to files by coordinating the storage across DataNodes. The NameNode is critical for the operation of HDFS; if it fails, the filesystem becomes inaccessible.
    NameNode。NameNode 是 HDFS 的中央组件，负责管理文件系统的元数据和命名空间。它跟踪文件位置，并通过协调各 DataNode 上的存储来管理对文件的访问。NameNode 对 HDFS 的运行至关重要；如果它故障，整个文件系统就无法访问。
  • DataNodes. DataNodes are the workers in the HDFS architecture. They store the actual data blocks that make up the files in HDFS. Each DataNode periodically sends heartbeats and block reports to the NameNode, ensuring that the system has an updated view of storage health and availability.
    DataNode。DataNode 是 HDFS 架构中的工作节点。它们存储构成 HDFS 中文件的实际数据块。每个 DataNode 定期向 NameNode 发送心跳和块报告，确保系统对存储健康状况和可用性有最新的视图。
  • Secondary NameNode. Despite its name, the secondary NameNode is not a backup for the NameNode. Instead, it works alongside the NameNode to manage the filesystem’s metadata. It periodically snapshots the metadata and applies the edit log, which helps reduce the recovery time in case of a NameNode failure.
    Secondary NameNode。尽管名字如此，Secondary NameNode 并不是 NameNode 的备份。相反，它与 NameNode 协同工作来管理文件系统的元数据。它定期对元数据做快照并应用编辑日志（edit log），这有助于在 NameNode 发生故障时缩短恢复时间。
  • Blocks. HDFS stores data in blocks, typically 128 MB in size, which are replicated across multiple DataNodes (usually three) for redundancy. This block-based storage system enables HDFS to handle large files efficiently, ensuring that even if a DataNode fails, the data remains available from another replica.
    块（Blocks）。HDFS 以块的形式存储数据，块大小通常为 128 MB，并在多个 DataNode（通常三个）之间复制以实现冗余。这种基于块的存储系统让 HDFS 能高效处理大文件，确保即使某个 DataNode 故障，数据仍可从另一个副本获得。
Page 230

When a client wants to read or write a file, it communicates with the NameNode to locate the DataNodes that hold the data blocks. For writing, the NameNode provides a list of DataNodes where the client should write the data blocks. Once written, the DataNodes replicate the blocks to other nodes as directed by the NameNode.

当客户端要读或写一个文件时，它与 NameNode 通信，以定位持有这些数据块的 DataNode。对于写操作，NameNode 提供一个 DataNode 列表，客户端应把数据块写到这些节点上。写入完成后，各 DataNode 会按照 NameNode 的指示把块复制到其他节点。

HDFS is rack aware, meaning it understands the physical layout of the nodes across different racks in a data center. The NameNode uses this information to make intelligent decisions about block placement, ensuring that replicas are distributed across different racks. This improves fault tolerance by ensuring that a rack failure doesn’t lead to data loss.

HDFS 是机架感知（rack aware）的，也就是说它了解数据中心内不同机架上节点的物理布局。NameNode 利用这些信息对块的放置做出智能决策，确保副本分布在不同机架上。这通过确保单个机架故障不会导致数据丢失，从而提升了容错性。

HDFS’s fault tolerance is achieved through data replication and periodic checks by the NameNode. If a DataNode fails, the NameNode initiates a replication of the affected blocks to other nodes to ensure data availability.

HDFS 的容错性是通过数据复制和 NameNode 的定期检查来实现的。如果某个 DataNode 故障，NameNode 会启动把受影响的块复制到其他节点的流程，以确保数据可用性。

Together, these components and features form a highly reliable, scalable distributed filesystem that is central to the Hadoop ecosystem. HDFS’s architecture is designed to handle large-scale data storage and retrieval across thousands of nodes, making it ideal for big data applications.

这些组件和特性共同构成了一个高可靠、可扩展的分布式文件系统，它在 Hadoop 生态中处于核心地位。HDFS 的架构设计用于跨数千个节点处理大规模数据存储和检索，因此非常适合大数据应用。

HDFS plays a critical role within the broader Hadoop ecosystem, offering essential storage capabilities for big data processing. However, when evaluating big data solutions, it’s important to consider other platforms as well. While the Hadoop ecosystem provides a comprehensive set of open source tools for managing and processing large datasets, cloud platforms like AWS offer managed services that can simplify deployment and scalability. Let’s now compare the Hadoop ecosystem with AWS, highlighting their differences, strengths, and use cases.

HDFS 在更广泛的 Hadoop 生态中扮演关键角色，为大数据处理提供不可或缺的存储能力。然而，在评估大数据方案时，同样重要的是考虑其他平台。虽然 Hadoop 生态提供了一整套用于管理和处理大型数据集的开源工具，但像 AWS 这样的云平台提供托管服务，可以简化部署和扩展。下面我们把 Hadoop 生态与 AWS 做一对比，突出它们的差异、长处和用例。

Hadoop ecosystem versus AWS

The Hadoop ecosystem is a comprehensive suite of tools designed for distributed data storage and processing across large clusters of computers. The core of Hadoop includes HDFS for scalable storage and MapReduce for parallel processing of large datasets. However, the ecosystem extends far beyond these two components to include tools such as Hive (for SQL-like querying of large datasets), Pig (a high-level scripting language for data analysis), HBase (a NoSQL database for real-time data), and YARN (for resource management). It also includes Apache Spark for in-memory data processing, Oozie for workflow scheduling, and ZooKeeper for distributed coordination.

Hadoop 生态是一整套工具，设计用于跨大型计算机集群进行分布式数据存储和处理。Hadoop 的核心包括用于可扩展存储的 HDFS 和用于大型数据集并行处理的 MapReduce。然而，这个生态远不止这两个组件，还包括 Hive（用于对大型数据集做类 SQL 查询）、Pig（一种用于数据分析的高级脚本语言）、HBase（一种用于实时数据的 NoSQL 数据库）以及 YARN（用于资源管理）。它还包括用于内存数据处理的 Apache Spark、用于工作流调度的 Oozie，以及用于分布式协调的 ZooKeeper。

AWS provides fully managed equivalents for most Hadoop services, eliminating much of the operational overhead. AWS services like Amazon S3 for scalable object storage, Amazon EMR for running Hadoop and Spark clusters, Amazon Athena for interactive query service, and AWS Glue for ETL operations all offer more integrated solutions with scaling, cost management, and security features. Table 8-1 presents a comparison of Hadoop services and their AWS counterparts.

AWS 为大多数 Hadoop 服务提供了全托管的等价物，省去了大量运维开销。像 Amazon S3（可扩展对象存储）、Amazon EMR（运行 Hadoop 和 Spark 集群）、Amazon Athena（交互式查询服务）和 AWS Glue（ETL 操作）这些 AWS 服务，都提供了更集成化的方案，并附带扩展、成本管理和安全特性。表 8-1 对比了 Hadoop 服务及其对应的 AWS 服务。

Hadoop ecosystem serviceDescriptionCorresponding AWS serviceComparison
HDFSDistributed filesystem for large-scale dataAmazon S3/EMRFS (built on top of S3)S3 is a scalable object store that is easier to manage than HDFS, with pay-as-you-go pricing.
MapReduceParallel processing of dataAmazon EMREMR supports MapReduce and automates cluster management, offering flexibility in instance types.
HiveDistributed data warehouse for online analytical processing (OLAP)Amazon RedshiftRedshift offers a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse that is optimized for OLAP and easier to scale.
PigHigh-level data analysis languageAWS GlueGlue offers serverless ETL with integrated workflow capabilities, replacing the manual setup of Pig.
