表 8-1。Hadoop 生态系统与 AWS 服务对比。HDFS（面向大规模数据的分布式文件系统）对应 Amazon S3/EMRFS（构建于 S3 之上）：S3 是可扩展对象存储，比 HDFS 更易管理，采用按需付费定价。MapReduce（数据并行处理）对应 Amazon EMR：EMR 支持 MapReduce 并自动化集群管理，在实例类型上提供灵活性。Hive（用于在线分析处理 OLAP 的分布式数据仓库）对应 Amazon Redshift：Redshift 提供全托管、PB 级数据仓库，针对 OLAP 优化且更易扩展。Pig（高级数据分析语言）对应 AWS Glue：Glue 提供无服务器 ETL 并集成工作流能力，取代了 Pig 的手工搭建。Presto（对大型数据集做类 SQL 查询）对应 Amazon Athena：Athena 是无服务器查询服务，无需预置基础设施即可对 S3 做 SQL 查询。HBase（用于实时分析的 NoSQL 数据库）对应 EMR 上的 HBase：EMR 上的 HBase 提供托管的 Hadoop 框架，类似于需手动扩展的自管 HBase。YARN（集群计算的资源管理器）对应 Amazon EMR/ECS：EMR 简化 YARN 管理；ECS 提供容器编排，把集群管理抽象掉。ZooKeeper（分布式应用协调）对应 AWS AppConfig：ZooKeeper 用于 Hadoop 和 Kafka 的元数据管理；AppConfig 用于 AWS 上的配置管理。Oozie（工作流调度）对应 AWS Step Functions：Step Functions 提供无服务器编排，与 AWS 服务集成更好，适用于 ETL 和工作流，优于 Oozie 的工作流管理。Sqoop（Hadoop 与关系数据库之间的结构化数据传输）对应 AWS Database Migration Service（DMS）：DMS 提供全托管服务，把各种数据库（关系型和非关系型）的数据迁移到云端，支持实时或批量迁移（类似 Sqoop），并附带云集成的额外特性。Flume（把来自各种来源的非结构化数据持续实时流入 Hadoop）对应 Amazon Kinesis：Kinesis 支持面向分析和流应用的实时数据接入与处理，相比 Flume 的手工流式搭建提供全托管服务。Spark（内存数据处理）对应 Amazon EMR 上的 Spark：EMR 支持运行 Spark 作业，相比 Hadoop 原生 Spark 搭建提供更多灵活性和管理选项。
Page 232

This comparison highlights how AWS provides more integrated, scalable alternatives to traditional Hadoop services, often with reduced operational overhead. We’ll be discussing these related AWS services more in Part II.

这一对比凸显了 AWS 如何为传统 Hadoop 服务提供更集成、更可扩展的替代方案，并且往往运维开销更低。我们将在第二部分更多地讨论这些相关 AWS 服务。

Apache Kafka: Distributed Message Queue

Apache Kafka is an open source distributed event-streaming platform capable of handling trillions of events a day in real time. As a highly reliable, scalable messaging system, Kafka can process millions of records per second, making it ideal for event-driven architectures, real-time analytics, and complex data pipelines. Here are some key features of Kafka:

Apache Kafka 是一个开源的分布式事件流平台，能够实时处理每天数万亿个事件。作为一个高可靠、可扩展的消息系统，Kafka 每秒可以处理数百万条记录，因此非常适合事件驱动架构、实时分析和复杂数据管道。下面是 Kafka 的一些关键特性：

  • Scalability. Kafka’s partitioning mechanism allows it to scale horizontally by distributing data across multiple nodes. This architecture supports high throughput and can handle large volumes of data.
    可扩展性。Kafka 的分区机制通过把数据分布到多个节点上，使其能够横向扩展。这种架构支持高吞吐量，并能处理海量数据。
  • Durability and reliability. Kafka ensures data durability by persisting messages on disk and replicating them across multiple brokers. This replication guarantees that even in the event of a broker failure, data is not lost.
    持久性与可靠性。Kafka 通过把消息持久化到磁盘、并在多个代理之间复制来确保数据持久。这种复制保证了即使某个代理故障，数据也不会丢失。
  • Fault tolerance. Kafka is designed to handle failures gracefully. In the event of a broker failure, Kafka’s replication mechanism ensures that another broker can take over the failed broker’s responsibilities without data loss.
    容错性。Kafka 被设计为优雅地处理故障。当某个代理故障时，Kafka 的复制机制确保另一个代理能够接管故障代理的职责，而不丢失数据。
  • High throughput. Kafka’s design is optimized for high throughput, making it capable of processing millions of records per second. This makes Kafka ideal for real-time data pipelines and event-driven architectures.
    高吞吐量。Kafka 的设计针对高吞吐量做了优化，使其每秒能处理数百万条记录。这使 Kafka 成为实时数据管道和事件驱动架构的理想选择。

Kafka architecture

Figure 8-9 presents Kafka’s components and architecture.

图 8-9 展示了 Kafka 的组件和架构。

Page 233

Let’s look at these components in more detail:

下面我们更详细地看看这些组件：

  • Producers. Producers are responsible for pushing data (records) into Kafka topics. They send data to the Kafka brokers, which manage partitioning and replicating the data across the cluster.
    生产者（Producers）。生产者负责把数据（记录）推送到 Kafka 主题。它们把数据发送到 Kafka 代理，由代理管理跨集群的分区和数据复制。
  • Consumers. Consumers read data from Kafka topics. They subscribe to one or more topics and consume records in the order they are stored in the partitions.
    消费者（Consumers）。消费者从 Kafka 主题读取数据。它们订阅一个或多个主题，并按照记录在分区中存储的顺序来消费记录。
  • Schema Registry. Schema Registry is a service that manages and enforces the schemas used by Kafka producers and consumers. It ensures that data is written in a consistent format, preventing compatibility issues between different versions of data structures as they evolve over time.
    Schema Registry。Schema Registry 是一项服务，负责管理并强制实施 Kafka 生产者和消费者所使用的模式。它确保数据以一致的格式写入，防止数据结构随时间演进时不同版本之间出现兼容性问题。
  • Brokers. Kafka brokers are the servers that manage the persistence and replication of data. Each broker stores data in partitions, which are the basic units of scalability in Kafka. Partitions allow Kafka to scale horizontally by distributing data across multiple nodes.
    代理（Brokers）。Kafka 代理是负责管理数据持久化和复制的服务器。每个代理把数据存储在分区中，分区是 Kafka 中可扩展性的基本单元。分区让 Kafka 能够通过把数据分布到多个节点上来横向扩展。
  • Coordinator. ZooKeeper used to manage the coordination of Kafka brokers in the cluster. It handled tasks such as leader election for partitions, cluster configuration, and metadata management. Recent versions of Kafka have replaced ZooKeeper with Apache Kafka Raft (KRaft) for consensus protocol and metadata management.
    协调者（Coordinator）。ZooKeeper 过去负责管理集群中 Kafka 代理之间的协调。它处理诸如分区选主、集群配置和元数据管理等任务。Kafka 的近期版本已经用 Apache Kafka Raft（KRaft）取代 ZooKeeper，用于共识协议和元数据管理。
Page 234
  • Topics. A Kafka topic is a category or feed name to which records are stored and published. Topics in Kafka are partitioned to allow data to be distributed across multiple brokers. Each partition is an ordered, immutable sequence of records that is continually appended to a log.
    主题（Topics）。Kafka 主题是一类记录被存储和发布到其中的类别或订阅源名称。Kafka 中的主题被分区，以便把数据分布到多个代理上。每个分区是一个有序、不可变的记录序列，不断地追加到日志中。
  • Partitions. Kafka partitions enable parallel processing of records within a topic. Each partition can be hosted on different brokers, allowing Kafka to scale horizontally and handle massive amounts of data. Partitions are also the units of replication in Kafka, ensuring data durability and fault tolerance.
    分区（Partitions）。Kafka 分区支持在一个主题内并行处理记录。每个分区可以托管在不同代理上，让 Kafka 能够横向扩展并处理海量数据。分区也是 Kafka 中复制的单元，确保数据持久性和容错性。
  • Keys. In Kafka, the key plays a crucial role in determining which partition a record is sent to within a topic. When a producer sends a record, it can specify a key. Kafka uses this key, along with a hashing function, to map the record to a specific partition. This ensures that records with the same key always go to the same partition, preserving the order of records for that key.
    键（Keys）。在 Kafka 中，键在决定一条记录被发往主题内哪个分区方面起着关键作用。生产者发送记录时可以指定一个键。Kafka 使用这个键以及一个哈希函数，把记录映射到特定分区。这确保具有相同键的记录总是进入同一个分区，从而保留该键对应记录的顺序。
Kafka appends messages to a partition in the exact order they are sent by a producer. If a producer sends message M1 before message M2 to the same partition, M1 will receive a lower offset than M2, ensuring that it appears earlier in the log. It’s important to note that this ordering guarantee applies only within individual partitions. Users can manage partitioning strategies to make use of this ordered delivery across different data segments.
Kafka 按照生产者发送消息的确切顺序把消息追加到分区中。如果生产者向同一分区先发送消息 M1、再发送消息 M2，那么 M1 的偏移量会比 M2 小，从而确保它在日志中出现得更早。需要注意的是，这种顺序保证只在单个分区内成立。用户可以管理分区策略，以便在不同数据段之间利用这种有序投递。

Kafka’s configuration levels

Kafka offers several configuration levels for fine-tuning the system to meet specific needs:

Kafka 提供若干配置级别，用于对系统做精细调优以满足特定需求：

  • Replication factor. This level determines the number of copies of a partition that Kafka will maintain across different brokers. Higher replication increases fault tolerance but also requires more storage and network resources.
    副本因子。这个级别决定 Kafka 跨不同代理维护一个分区的多少份副本。副本越多，容错性越强，但也需要更多存储和网络资源。
  • Acknowledgments. Producers can configure the level of acknowledgment they require from the brokers. For example, a setting of acks=all ensures that a message is considered successfully written only when all in-sync replicas acknowledge it, enhancing reliability at the cost of higher latency.
    确认（Acknowledgments）。生产者可以配置它要求代理给出何种级别的确认。例如，设置 acks=all 可确保只有当所有同步副本都确认时，一条消息才被视为成功写入，从而以更高延迟为代价增强可靠性。
Page 235
  • Retention policies. Kafka allows configuration of how long records are retained in the topics. Retention can be based on time (e.g., seven days) or size (e.g., 100 GB), ensuring that only relevant data is kept for more effective storage management.
    保留策略。Kafka 允许配置记录在主题中保留多长时间。保留可以基于时间（例如 7 天）或基于大小（例如 100 GB），确保只保留相关数据，从而更有效地管理存储。
  • Compression. Message compression in Kafka reduces the amount of data that is transmitted over the network and stored on disk. Different compression algorithms like gzip, snappy, and lz4 can be configured based on the use case.
    压缩。Kafka 中的消息压缩减少了网络传输和磁盘存储的数据量。可以根据用例配置 gzip、snappy、lz4 等不同压缩算法。

Kafka provides strong messaging guarantees that ensure the reliable delivery of messages in distributed systems. These guarantees are crucial for maintaining data consistency and integrity across complex data pipelines:

Kafka 提供强有力的消息投递保证，确保在分布式系统中可靠地投递消息。这些保证对于在复杂数据管道中维持数据一致性和完整性至关重要：

  • At-most-once delivery. Messages are delivered to consumers at most once, meaning they may be lost but are never delivered more than once. This is the default setting when no retries or acknowledgments are configured.
    至多一次投递。消息至多被投递给消费者一次，也就是说它们可能丢失，但绝不会被投递多次。当没有配置重试或确认时，这是默认设置。
  • At-least-once delivery. Every message is delivered at least once. This means that even in the event of a failure, the message will eventually reach the consumer, though duplicates may occur. This guarantee is often used when data loss is unacceptable, and duplicate messages can be handled by the application logic. To manage the potential duplicates, applications consuming messages in an at-least-once delivery setup should implement idempotency in their processing logic.
    至少一次投递。每条消息至少被投递一次。这意味着即使发生故障，消息最终也会到达消费者，尽管可能出现重复。当数据丢失不可接受、而重复消息可以由应用逻辑处理时，常使用这种保证。为了应对可能的重复，在“至少一次”投递模式下消费消息的应用，应当在其处理逻辑中实现幂等性。
  • Exactly-once delivery. Exactly-once semantics (EOS) in Kafka ensure that each message is delivered to the consumer exactly once, without any duplicates, even in the face of failures. This is achieved through Kafka’s idempotent producers and transactional APIs, which maintain atomicity across multiple partitions and topics. EOS is particularly valuable in systems where data integrity is critical, such as financial transactions.
    恰好一次投递。Kafka 中的恰好一次语义（EOS）确保每条消息被恰好一次地投递给消费者、没有任何重复，即使在发生故障时也是如此。这是通过 Kafka 的幂等生产者和事务 API 实现的，它们跨多个分区和主题维持原子性。EOS 在数据完整性至关重要的系统（例如金融交易）中尤其有价值。
An operation is idempotent if applying it multiple times has the same effect as applying it once. For example, a consumer might keep track of processed message IDs to prevent processing duplicates. This approach ensures that repeated messages do not result in unintended side effects, maintaining data integrity in applications that require precise processing.
如果一个操作多次应用与应用一次效果相同，它就是幂等的。例如，消费者可以记录已处理过的消息 ID，以防止重复处理。这种做法确保重复消息不会产生意料之外的副作用，在需要精确处理的应用中维持数据完整性。
Page 236

These messaging guarantees, along with Kafka’s robust fault tolerance and scalability, make it a reliable choice for building distributed data streaming and processing systems. Kafka’s ability to handle large-scale data streams with low latency has made it a cornerstone in modern distributed systems.

这些消息投递保证，加上 Kafka 强健的容错性和可扩展性，使其成为构建分布式数据流和处理系统的可靠选择。Kafka 以低延迟处理大规模数据流的能力，已使其成为现代分布式系统的基石。

AWS offers Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (MSK) and Amazon Kinesis, which are managed services designed for real-time data streaming. MSK simplifies running Apache Kafka on AWS, while Kinesis provides tools for collecting, processing, and analyzing streaming data. Both services enable scalable, reliable data processing. We will explore them further in Chapter 12.
AWS 提供 Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka（MSK）和 Amazon Kinesis，二者都是为实时数据流设计的托管服务。MSK 简化了在 AWS 上运行 Apache Kafka 的工作，而 Kinesis 提供收集、处理和分析流数据的工具。这两项服务都支持可扩展、可靠的数据处理。我们将在第 12 章进一步探讨它们。

Comparing HDFS and Kafka

Both HDFS and Kafka are designed to handle large volumes of data efficiently. We compare their features in Table 8-2.

HDFS 和 Kafka 都旨在高效处理海量数据。我们在表 8-2 中对比它们的特性。

FeatureHDFSKafka
Core functionDistributed file storageMessage queue/event-streaming platform
Use caseBig data storage, large-scale processingReal-time messaging, event sourcing
Data modelFilesStreams of records
PerformanceHigh throughput, optimized for large filesHigh throughput, optimized for message passing
ScalabilityLinear scalability with more nodesScales horizontally with topics and partitions
Fault toleranceReplication across nodesReplication within and across clusters
表 8-2。HDFS 与 Kafka 对比。核心功能：HDFS 是分布式文件存储；Kafka 是消息队列/事件流平台。用例：HDFS 用于大数据存储、大规模处理；Kafka 用于实时消息传递、事件溯源。数据模型：HDFS 是文件；Kafka 是记录流。性能：两者都是高吞吐，HDFS 针对大文件优化，Kafka 针对消息传递优化。可扩展性：HDFS 随节点增多线性扩展；Kafka 随主题和分区横向扩展。容错性：HDFS 跨节点复制；Kafka 在集群内和跨集群复制。

Both HDFS and Kafka are powerful open source technologies that cater to specific needs within distributed systems. HDFS is ideal for applications requiring large-scale data storage and processing, while Kafka is suited to applications that need robust, real-time data processing and messaging capabilities. Choosing between HDFS and Kafka depends on your organization’s specific data management and processing needs.

HDFS 和 Kafka 都是强大的开源技术，分别满足分布式系统中的特定需求。HDFS 非常适合需要大规模数据存储和处理的应用，而 Kafka 则适合那些需要强健的实时数据处理和消息传递能力的应用。在 HDFS 和 Kafka 之间如何选择，取决于你组织具体的数据管理和处理需求。

Conclusion

The architectural designs and patterns discussed in this chapter provide a comprehensive toolkit for building scalable, maintainable, efficient systems. CDC offers a mechanism for ensuring that data is always up to date across distributed environments, while the pub/sub architecture facilitates decoupled communication between system components. Big data architectures like lambda, kappa, and data lake offer robust solutions for processing and analyzing vast amounts of data. Meanwhile, Kafka and HDFS serve as foundational technologies in distributed systems, each excelling in their domains: real-time event streaming and large-scale data storage, respectively.

本章讨论的架构设计与模式为构建可扩展、可维护、高效的系统提供了一套全面的工具箱。CDC 提供了一种机制，确保分布式环境中的数据始终是最新的；而发布/订阅架构则促进了系统组件之间解耦的通信。lambda、kappa、数据湖等大数据架构为处理和分析海量数据提供了稳健方案。与此同时，Kafka 和 HDFS 作为分布式系统中的基础技术，各自在自己的领域中表现出色：分别是实时事件流处理和大规模数据存储。

Page 237

By understanding and leveraging the architectural patterns and technologies discussed in the last sections of this chapter, organizations can build systems that not only meet current needs but also are adaptable to future challenges. The flexibility, scalability, and fault tolerance offered by these design patterns ensure that your system architecture can evolve in tandem with growing business demands and technological advancements. Keep in mind that design patterns are constantly changing, and there is no comprehensive list—we’ve covered only the tip of the iceberg. These architecture patterns are like guidelines that you can follow, but you do not need to completely adhere to them. Use whatever makes sense for your business requirements and do not force a design pattern to your requirements. As technology advances, new patterns and strategies will continue to emerge, shaping the future of system architecture and design.

通过理解并运用本章后几节讨论的架构模式和技术，组织可以构建出不仅满足当前需求、还能适应未来挑战的系统。这些设计模式所提供的灵活性、可扩展性和容错性，确保你的系统架构能够与不断增长的业务需求和技术进步同步演进。请记住，设计模式在不断变化，并不存在一份完备的清单——我们所讲的只是冰山一角。这些架构模式就像可以遵循的指南，但你不必完全拘泥于它们。凡是对你的业务需求合理的就采用，不要把某种设计模式硬套到你的需求上。随着技术进步，新的模式和策略将不断涌现，塑造系统架构与设计的未来。
